2. Experimental Section
2.1. Smelting Process
Three smelting experiments of Fe-15Mn-<sup>x</sup>Al-C (<sup>x</sup> = 1, 3, 5) low-
density steel with different Al contents were conducted under
laboratory conditions. The first smelting experiment process is
as follows: First, iron powder (700 g) and ferrous oxalate
( \mathrm { F e C } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } _ { 4 } { \cdot } \mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O }
, 1.575 g) are placed in an alumina crucible and
then placed in a tubular furnace for heating. When the tubular
furnace was heated to 1873 K, kept for 40 min, and then deoxi
dizer was added. First, 225 g of ferromanganese was added and
kept for 20 min. Then 11 g of aluminum particles were added
that were wrapped in the pure iron sheet and kept for 60 min.
Finally, the sample was cooled to room temperature in a tubular
furnace. The operating steps and the amount of ferromanganese
added in the three groups of experiments were consistent. The
mass of pure aluminum particles added to the second and third
groups was 28 and 48 g, respectively. The chemical composition
of iron powder, ferromanganese, and aluminum particles is
shown in .
2.2. Analytical Methods
The chemical composition of three steels was detected using
chemical analysis methods. The content of T.O and T.N was mea-
sured by a carbon sulfur analyzer. The carbon sulfur analyzer
detected the content of C and S. Inductively coupled plasma mass
spectrometry measured the content of Al, Si, Ti, Mn, and P.
The inclusions in the experimental samples were observed in
two methods. 1) Metallographic observation. Solid steel was cut
into cylinders using an electric discharge wire-cutting machine.
Subsequently, metallographic sandpaper and metallographic
polishing paste were used to process the sample into a mirror
surface. 2) Preparation of inclusion powder by nonaqueous sol-
vent electrolytic separation. After electrolytic separation, a mag-
net was used to separate the inclusion particles from the solution
containing ethanol and collect them on a carbon strip.<sup>[19–21]</sup>

for field-emission scanning electron microscopy (Model:
ZEISS ΣIGMA HD) with energy dispersive spectrometer

of inclusions. The size, type, and number of inclusions were
